findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: The plumbing line under the triple sink in the back is still observed to be leaking. Discussed with PIC, a new triple sink has been ordered. findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: All Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) certificates have expired. Discussed CFPM course and proctoring with person in charge (PIC). The PIC had 2 of the same educational sheet regarding accredited programs from the Sangamon County Department of Public Health from previous inspectors. All facilities serving food are required to have a CFPM on staff and scheduled during all shifts. CFPMs decrease the incidence of a food-borne illnesses, decrease the number of critical violations, and demonstrate proper food safety practices to their staff.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two sanitizer buckets located at the barista station to be tested at 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Violations from the original inspection dated 11/15/2022 have begun to occur in the facility again. These priority/priority foundation items had been corrected during the previous follow-up. Operator was aware of the follow-up scheduled for today and was aware of the corrective actions required to be in compliance with 2017 FDA Food Code. Due to the recurrence of priority/priority foundation violations and apparent lack of active managerial control at the facility during the inspection today, an additional follow-up is being issued for January 16, 2023 (due to 01/05/2023 falling on a Sunday). Ensure that person-in-charge is actively managing employees and preventing continued violations. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. Pf

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the hand front hand sink under the “Coffee & Espresso” sign was visibly soiled with coffee and a long spoon used for stirring product was observed sitting in the hand sink. As discussed during prior inspections, hand sinks may ONLY be used for HAND WASHING and NO OTHER PURPOSES. Dumping, filling and any other food preparation activities are not allowed in hand sinks. Ensure that hand sinks are used ONLY for hand washing and are not blocked by other items at ANY TIME. An additional follow-up is issued for December 27, 2022 (due to holiday scheduling). 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the ice scoop next to the ice bin under the “Coffee & Espresso” sign to be stored in a visibly soiled blender cup which was the same violation as during the previous routine inspection for which follow-up was occurring today. Inspector discussed with person-in-charge why this was occurring. Inspector was advised that the container is cleaned every 4 hours. However, the presence of brown residue and debris in the container which the ice scoop is stored in indicates that cleaning and sanitizing of this container is not occurring on a sufficient basis. The ice scoop is a food contact surface directly contacting ice throughout the service period. As such, it must remain clean and free of contaminants and a visibly soiled container is not sufficient. Ensure that food is protected from contamination by storing utensils in clean, dry locations free of visible residue and debris. Inspector will return on 12/19/2022 (due to weekend scheduling) to check on the storage of the ice scoop. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a can of whipped cream sitting out on the counter under the “Coffee & Espresso” counter. The can had no apparent date marking but operator states that they go through it quickly and it has not been out for long. The temperature of the can was 68 degrees F at the lowest point on the can where liquid was present. The can is clearly marked “Perishable” and “Keep Refrigerated”. Operator removed the can from the counter and discarded without further discussion. Ensure that foods which are required to be held at 41 degrees F or less are maintained at that temperature or lower. As the product was voluntarily discarded during the inspection, corrected on site and no further follow-up is required for this violation.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
The facility has several priority/priority foundation violations and repeat violations from previous inspections. Person-in-charge has failed to ensure that hand washing sinks remain accessible and are used for no other purposes which inhibits operators from washing hands as frequently as required to provide a safe food operation. Food has not been protected from contamination throughout the course of operations. A follow-up is being issued for 30-days to evaluate the operation and ensure that person-in-charge is properly managing compliance with priority and priority foundation violations. Ensure that all priority/priority foundation violations are corrected and the facility remains in compliance. Inspector will return on 12/15/2022 to check on the status of these corrective actions. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. Pf

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.comment:

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
On arrival, hand washing sink was observed to have a spoon and frosting in it. The hand washing sink may not be used for dumping, filling or any other purposes except hand washing. This is a repeat violation from previous inspection on 10/13/2021. A warning letter/notice to comply will be issued. A 10-day follow-up is being issued for 11/28/2022 (due to Thanksgiving scheduling)  to ensure compliance.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the ice scoop at the front ice bin under the “coffee & espresso” sign to be stored in a visibly soiled plastic blender container. Operator was advised the the container for the ice scoop must be cleaned every four hours or whenever soiled, whichever occurs first. Ice in the bin was observed to have brown food residue assumed to be coffee. Ice scoop was removed from the container and the container was cleaned. Ice was removed from the bin. Bin was cleaned and refilled. Corrected on site. No further follow-up required at this time. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Using a brown paper towel from the nearby hand sink, inspector was able to remove a significantly thick layer of mold from the bottom edge of the baffle in the ice machine. The baffle is a food-contact surface and must be clean to sight and touch at all times. Ensure that the ice machine is cleaned regularly to prevent the accumulation of residue and debris. A follow-up is being issued for 11/28/2022 (due to Thanksgiving scheduling) to ensure compliance. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Upon arrival to the facility, inspector observed wet wiping cloths sitting on counters throughout the facility including the front register counter, the counter near the dump sink under the “coffee and espresso sign” and the drive thru. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution when not actively being used. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer between uses or paper towels are used and disposed of as needed. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
The handle of the scoop in the powdered sugar tub at the rear of the facility is observed to be stored handle down in the powdered sugar. The handle must be stored out of the food to prevent contamination. Ensure that food handles are not contacting food in containers during storage. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:

A warning letter/notice to comply will be issued. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned often enough to prevent the accumulation of residue and debris on these surfaces. 

The hood above the fryer is observed to be soiled with dust and debris. Ensure that this surface is cleaned at a rate sufficient enough to preclude the accumulation of dust and grease. The current cleaning frequency is not sufficient to preclude the accumulation of debris and poses and contamination hazard to the food being processed beneath it. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Signed reporting agreements were not available for management or staff at the time of inspection. Employee health policy was said to be part of onboarding process, but information was not readily available during the inspection. GM made copies of the employee health reporting agreement. Management and staff working at the time of inspection reviewed the document and signed it for the facility records. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff until proof of digital verification is available.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Handwashing sink in donut prep area was used as a dump sink. Employee was advised on proper use of handwashing sinks. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using any handwashing sinks as dump sinks.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solutions in sani-buckets at front counter and drive thru were observed at 100ppm. Fresh sanitizer solutions were provided at 200ppm. Ensure sanitizer solutions are changed as needed.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Stem of food thermometer used to check dough was soiled with stuck on food debris in the storage holster. GM noted the thermometer is cleaned at shift change twice a day. Ensure the stem of the thermometer is wiped with sanitizer solution between uses. As a food contact surface, the stem of the thermometer needs to also be washed, rinsed, and sanitized at 4hr intervals assuming raw dough is a TCS food. If dough is a non-TCS food, the stem needs to be at minimum washed, rinsed, and sanitized at the end of operations daily.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Door handles and the bottom inside the two door cooler in back storage ware soiled with food debris.
-Underside of sprinkle drawer handles were soiled with hardened icing buildup.
Clean the aforementioned general surfaces as needed and maintain them clean.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Floor at the drive thru was soiled with general debris accumulation under the cooler, cash register counter, and doughnut storage. clean the floor under equipment at the drive thru.
-Caulk at the 3 part sink was soiled with mold. If cleaning/disinfecting does not remove mold, then replace the caulk (see general comments for additional information).
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
